transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-20 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~63 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Asha Rao (CTO - DataFort), Ben Malik (Infra Eng), Priya Singh (Security), Jay (Ops)
Shared artifacts: rwd-offline-install-checklist.pdf (link), s3://redwood-offline-artifacts/datafort-bundle-v1.tar.gz (note: will provide via secure transfer), driver-compatibility-matrix.xlsx

[00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. We're planning a deep dive on the on-prem airgapped install, offline licensing, and GPU driver compatibility. Marco will drive the technical bits. Quick intros?
[00:12] Asha Rao: Hi, Asha here, CTO at DataFort. We're evaluating on-prem for PII workloads, so airgap plus HSM/KMS integration is must.
[00:20] Ben Malik: Ben - infra. We run mixed NVIDIA A100 and some older V100s in a colo. Want to understand runtime perf tradeoffs and any special driver reqs.
[00:29] Priya Singh: Priya - security. SOC2 in flight, need audit logs and key management details.
[00:35] Marco Diaz: Marco from Redwood SE. I'll go through artifact delivery, drivers, quantization artifacts, and runtime configuration.
[00:42] Jay: Jay - operations, will own install coordination.
[00:45] Lena Park: Great, agenda: artifacts and delivery, license & offline activation model, driver/CUDA/cuDNN compatibility, runtime perf knobs (KV cache, batching, quant), and a short Q&A.

[03:10] Marco Diaz: Kicking off - artifact bundle: we package the inference runtime, model binaries (quantized and fp16 if available), a lightweight package manager, and a verification manifest with sha256 sums. For airgapped installs we produce a tarball and an instructions PDF. We'll also include the offline license file and an activation tool that runs locally.
[03:45] Ben Malik: When you say "model binaries", are these Redwood-curated open models or customer-provided fine-tuned checkpoints? We need to avoid any external pull.
[03:52] Marco Diaz: Good call. We can include either. For your PII workflows customers typically provide their own checkpoints. We'll include a loader that points to a local path; we don't reach out to the internet. The bundle includes both base and quantized variants if you've chosen Redwood quantization profiles.

[06:05] Priya Singh: On licensing: offline activation — how does that work for airgapped environments? We can't have a callback.
[06:12] Marco Diaz: We have two options: 1) Static signed license file per install (recommended for fully airgapped) that the customer places in the install dir; it contains the seat count, support window, and expiry and is signed by Redwood's private key. 2) Time-limited activation codes where you run an offline activation tool that validates against a pre-shared offline token. For SOC and audited environments we usually do option 1.
[06:45] Priya Singh: Are private keys ever on the customer side? KMS integration concerns me.
[06:50] Marco Diaz: No private Redwood keys are stored on customer hosts. We sign the license server-side and provide the signed artifact. For runtime encryption we support customer-managed KMS—local HSM integration is possible but we typically do envelope encryption where keys are in your KMS and runtime references them. We'll send the KMS integration docs.

[09:00] Asha Rao: Driver compatibility: we have mixed NVIDIA fleet - A100, A40, V100. Do you have a strict driver/CUDA requirement? Upgrading is disruptive.
[09:10] Marco Diaz: We maintain a tested matrix. For the 2025.1 runtime the recommended stack is CUDA 11.8 with NVIDIA driver >=525.60 for best perf on A100; older drivers may work but you lose some kernel optimizations. For V100 we have tested with CUDA 10.2 and CUDA 11.x but the perf story differs. We'll share driver-compatibility-matrix.xlsx.
[09:42] Ben Malik: If we can't upgrade drivers on some hosts, can we run mixed clusters or route inference to compatible hosts?
[09:49] Marco Diaz: Yes, smart routing supports heterogeneous pools. You can tag machines by compatibility and Redwood's scheduler routes requests based on model variant and hardware profile. So older V100s can run fp16 or fp32 models while A100s handle int8/quantized fast paths. That said, some quantized kernels require newer drivers.

[12:30] Jay: Transfer logistics: how big is the bundle? We're constrained over airgap transfers (sneakernet).
[12:37] Marco Diaz: Typical full bundle with models is 40-200GB depending on model size and quantization. We can produce a slim bundle (runtime + minimal model) and a separate model tarball so you only transfer the pieces you need. We'll provide checksums and MD5/sha256.

[15:05] Asha Rao: Runtime perf knobs - batching and KV cache. Can you summarize best practices for low-latency endpoints?
[15:12] Marco Diaz: Sure. For latency-sensitive single-turn requests, set batching window small (1-10ms) and enable prefix KV caching only when you have repeated prefixes or chat workloads. Batching increases throughput but adds queuing latency; we tune concurrency and batch size. For long-context chat with KV cache, ensure your cache memory is sized for the KV cache so you avoid swapping. We expose metrics so you can see cache hit rates and tail latency.
[15:58] Ben Malik: What about memory for KV cache on multi-tenant hosts? We want memory isolation.
[16:05] Marco Diaz: You can reserve memory per container/slot and set a per-model KV cache soft limit. If the cache exceeds the limit it evicts LRU entries. We also support sharded KV cache across GPUs to keep per-host memory lower; the orchestration layer handles shard placement.

[18:40] Priya Singh: Quantization—how much perf gain, and what about accuracy regressions? We need to evaluate diffs on our eval sets.
[18:48] Marco Diaz: Typical int8 quant gives 2-4x throughput improvement and 2-3x lower memory vs fp16 for many large transformer models, but quality drop varies. We produce quantization profiles and recommend running your eval harnesses; we also provide a quality regression report for the model with our suggested prompts. For safety-critical outputs you can pin to fp16 for canaries and run canary traffic there.
[19:30] Asha Rao: Do you produce quantized artifacts in the bundle or do we run quantization locally?
[19:35] Marco Diaz: We can do either. For audited environments we often pre-quantize and ship the quantized artifact with its checksums so the artifact is immutable. If you prefer to control quantization locally, we provide the quant tooling and reproducible profiles.

[22:10] Ben Malik: Can we run performance regressions offline? We want to simulate 95th percentile latency with our traffic generator in an internal lab.
[22:18] Marco Diaz: Yes. We include a lightweight load generator and a perf harness that reports p50/p95/p99, token-per-second, and GPU utilization. You can run it with your traffic patterns and we recommend starting with synthetic single-user latency tests then scaling to burst tests.

[24:45] Jay: Regarding GPU drivers—do you require CUDA toolkit installed on the host, or is it containerized?
[24:53] Marco Diaz: We ship a container runtime optimized for the host. We require NVIDIA driver on the host; CUDA toolkit is not strictly necessary on host if you use our container images that bundle necessary CUDA runtime libs. For airgapped we provide images and a local registry tarball. Host driver presence is still required for kernel modules.

[27:00] Asha Rao: Networking—our cluster is completely isolated. How do you manage license renewals or support access?
[27:06] Marco Diaz: For renewals we use signed license files and an offline renewal workflow where you upload the license request file via a secure channel (e.g., SFTP or physical media) to Redwood, we sign a renewal license, and return it. Support can be via phone/email; for escalations we can do encrypted bundle transfers and we offer an on-prem support option to send an engineer on site.

[30:20] Priya Singh: Audit logs and telemetry—what leaves the box? We need to be explicit.
[30:27] Marco Diaz: Default is no telemetry out. We ship a telemetry opt-in. For on-prem customers you can enable periodic batched logs that are stored locally or pushed to your SIEM. We produce detailed audit logs for model loads, inference requests, and license activations that you can pipe to your ELK/Graylog.

[33:05] Ben Malik: About the scheduler—can we prioritize tenant A over B? We run internal apps and external clients on same infra.
[33:13] Marco Diaz: Yes, we support per-queue QoS, priority routing, and preemption policies. You can map workloads to reserved GPU pools and enforce throughput SLOs. The config is declarative in a YAML that we include in the bundle.

[35:50] Asha Rao: Any gotchas for mixed-driver fleets when using TFLOPS-heavy kernels?
[35:57] Marco Diaz: Some kernels are only available with newer driver+CUDA combos; you'll see fallback to slower kernels when on older drivers, which increases latency and reduces throughput. If you have a mixed fleet, expect the scheduler to route latency-sensitive traffic to the newer nodes. Also watch for NCCL versions when using multi-GPU collective ops—we'll list recommended NCCL versions.

[38:22] Jay: Security checklist — we need an itemized list for our compliance team.
[38:28] Marco Diaz: We'll attach our on-prem security checklist: OS hardening steps, processes for storing signed license files, KMS integration notes, recommended file permissions, and guidance on audit log retention.

[40:10] Priya Singh: For the HSM flow—we'd like to keep private keys in our HSM. Can runtime call our HSM for decryption ops?
[40:18] Marco Diaz: Yes, we support PKCS#11 interfaces for HSMs and you can configure the runtime to call your HSM for envelope key unwrap operations. We'll include example config snippets.

[42:30] Ben Malik: How do we validate the artifact bundle after transfer? Is there a reproducible verification?
[42:37] Marco Diaz: The bundle includes a manifest.json with file paths and sha256s, plus a signature file. The offline verification tool checks all checksums and validates the signature using an embedded Redwood public cert. We also include an ops checklist for transfer and verification.

[45:05] Asha Rao: Lessons from other customers — any surprises you recommend we watch for?
[45:12] Marco Diaz: A few: 1) driver mismatches cause the bulk of surprises; validate driver+NVIDIA driver module loads first. 2) KV cache sizing is commonly under-provisioned and leads to evictions impacting tail latency. 3) Quantization can expose prompt-sensitive regressions—run evals. And 4) ship checksums and test restores as part of your transfer validation.

[48:30] Lena Park: Quick pricing/licensing note — offline license is a per-seat (concurrent) model with optional 24x7 support. I'll follow up with formal options.

[50:05] Priya Singh: One question on metrics—do you store token-level costs and token latency breakdowns locally?
[50:12] Marco Diaz: Yes, the runtime emits token-level timing and cost estimates to local telemetry endpoints. In on-prem mode you can keep all telemetry local. We support per-route dashboards in the console but for airgapped installs we provide the dashboards as static HTML bundles and a local UI that reads local metrics.

[52:40] Ben Malik: For the performance harness, can it simulate KV-cache warmup patterns?
[52:47] Marco Diaz: It can; we include scripts to simulate prefix warmups and chat sessions to reproduce cold vs warm cache behaviors.

[55:10] Asha Rao: Ok, let's talk schedule — we want a pilot on 2 A100 hosts first. Can you support a pilot next month?
[55:20] Marco Diaz: Yes. If you confirm hostnames and a transfer window we'll package a pilot bundle and remote support plan.
[55:30] Lena Park: For next steps recap: Marco will share driver matrix, offline bundle checklist, and perf harness. I'll send pricing and license options. Asha to confirm pilot host list. Priya to send SOC2 questions.

[58:00] Jay: Quick micro question — GPU firmware updates are needed sometimes; do you support guidance or will you validate firmware?
[58:08] Marco Diaz: We provide firmware recommendations and a preflight script that checks BIOS/firmware versions. We don't automate firmware updates but will document steps and help validate post-update.

[60:30] Asha Rao: Great, this was useful. We'll review artifacts and circle back.
[60:40] Lena Park: Thanks everyone. We'll get the docs out by EOD tomorrow.
[60:46] Marco Diaz: Thanks, bye.

Meeting end.
